title: Confirming Activate moves the ticked parts back to the Active tab
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create three parts for this test, part A, part B and part C, and set all three inactive.
  • Give parts A, B and C part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists all three.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Inactive tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  3. Click Activate parts.
  4. Click the part A row.
  5. Click the part B row.
  6. Click Activate on the dark bar.
  7. Click Activate in the confirmation.
  8. Click the Active tab.
  9. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box again.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A, B and C are listed.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 4:

  • The part A row is ticked.

Step 5:

  • The bar reads 2 selected.

Step 6:

  • The "Activate parts?" confirmation opens and reads "2 parts selected."
  • Its lines read "These parts can be added to new work again." and "Existing records that use them stay as they are."
  • Its confirm button is a blue "Activate", with Cancel to its left.

Step 7:

  • A green message reads "2 parts updated."
  • Parts A and B leave the Inactive list at once, without a page reload, and part C is still listed.
  • Bulk mode ends and nothing is ticked.

Step 8:

  • The Active tab is selected.

Step 9:

  • The Active tab lists parts A and B.
  • Part C is not listed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10816 (Story 3, Activate Parts in Bulk), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S3-R4: “When the user confirms (Story 10), every ticked part becomes active and leaves the Inactive tab without a page reload.”
  • S3-R5: “The reactivated parts appear on the Active tab.”
  • S10-R3: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation is titled "Deactivate parts?" or "Activate parts?". Raised from the part dialog, it is titled "Deactivate part?" or "Activate part?".”
  • S10-R8: “For a reactivation from the bulk bar, the confirmation states "These parts can be added to new work again." ("This part ..." for one), followed by "Existing records that use them stay as they are." ("... that use it ..." for one).”
  • S10-R11: “The confirm button reads "Deactivate" in red for a deactivation and "Activate" in blue for a reactivation. Cancel sits to its left.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Bulk change, every part changed | "{n} parts updated." ("1 part updated." for one) | Success toast, fades on its own”
